govdocs-archive_org-nsia-AutopsyJFKPictu: This item — Autopsy JFK Pictures and X-rays: Aguilar and Weisberg — is a National Security Internet Archive file on the disputed evidence. The file’s full context is unclear. The autopsy materials remain controversial. The item is a fragment of the archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ConwayDebra_Con: Harold Weisberg’s letter to Debra and Tom Conway — November 1, 1996 — is a researcher’s note. The file belongs to the assassination archive. Weisberg wrote into his nineties. His papers are a treasure. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CubaniaBeligera: Jack Anderson’s Anti-Castro Units Threaten Terrorism covers exile militant groups. The columnist’s story belongs to the political archive. Miami exiles plotted against Castro for years. The story caused a stir. The threats were real. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HochPaulMemoran: Paul Hoch’s piece on the FBI investigation of Oswald’s use of 544 Camp Street is a researcher’s work. The address was a New Orleans mystery. The piece is sharp. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MottStewartRawl: Patrick J. Owens’s One Man’s Fortune: Stewart Rawlings Mott is a Detroit Free Press profile. Mott was the GM heir turned philanthropist. The profile is rich. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
the-wagner-story-book-firelight-tales-of: William Henry Frost retells the stories of Wagner's great operas — the Ring, Lohengrin, Tannhäuser, and more — as fireside tales for young readers. Gods, heroes, dragons, and doomed love unfold in prose versions of the mighty music dramas. A wonderful first doorway into Wagner for children not yet ready for the opera house.
schwatka-s-search-sledging-in-the-arctic: William Henry Gilder accompanied Lieutenant Frederick Schwatka's 1878 expedition into the Arctic, sledging hundreds of miles in search of records from Sir John Franklin's lost expedition. His account of cold, hunger, and endurance among the Inuit is a classic of polar literature. A gripping true story of one of the great searches of the age.
the-duenna-a-comic-opera: Sheridan's sparkling comic opera — with music by his father-in-law Thomas Linley — weaves mistaken identities and young love through a Spanish setting. Its wit and melody made it one of the great hits of the London stage. Readers can enjoy the libretto's verbal fireworks even without the music.
voyages-of-peter-esprit-radisson-being-a: Pierre Radisson — the daredevil coureur de bois — recounts his incredible travels among the Indigenous peoples of the Great Lakes in the 1600s. Captured, adopted, escaped: his adventures read like fiction but helped open the fur trade. One of the most thrilling true narratives of early Canada.
history-of-the-ottawa-and-chippewa-india: Andrew J. Blackbird — himself an Ottawa chief's son — wrote this history of the Ottawa and Chippewa Indians of Michigan, adding a grammar of their language and his own reminiscences. A rare nineteenth-century Indigenous voice telling its people's story in its own terms. Invaluable for historians and deeply moving for any reader.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abdera: This 1913 reference piece on Abdera, the Thracian city of Democritus and Protagoras. Laughing philosophers came from its walls. The entry notes its coins and ruins. An old Greek town, remembered for its wise men. Its air was said to breed dull wits and sharp tongues.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abraham-a-san: This 1913 reference article on Abraham a Sancta Clara — the witty Augustinian preacher of old Vienna. Nikolaus Scheid celebrates his humor and fire. His sermons mixed jokes with judgment. Austria's beloved pulpit voice. His Judas the Arch-Rogue made all Vienna laugh.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abraham-ben-m: A 1913 entry on Abraham ibn Ezra — the wandering Jewish scholar, poet, and Bible critic. Anthony Maas honors his restless genius. Spain, Italy, and England all knew his staff. A medieval mind of the first rank. His Bible notes still puzzle and delight scholars.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agra: A 1913 entry on Agra — the Indian archdiocese of the Taj city. Stanislaus O'Brien traces its mission story. The Mogul capital became a Catholic see. Its cathedral faces the marble tomb. Faith beside the world's wonder. Its seminary trains the Indian clergy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexandre-rod: This 1913 reference piece on Alexandre Rodrigues Ferreira — the great traveler of Brazil's wilds — tells his tale. Jeremiah Ford follows his long trek. He sailed the Amazon and its branches. Lisbon's museum keeps his finds. His maps opened the deep interior. Brazil honors its first field man of science.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alfonso-de-za: A 1913 entry on Alfonso de Zamora — the converted rabbi, master of Hebrew. Anthony Maas praises his scholarship. His work aided the Complutensian Bible. Ximenes valued his learning. A bridge between synagogue and Church. His psalter aided the Hebrew scholars. His fame rests on the polyglot pages.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alvaro-de-men: This 1913 reference piece on Mendaña — the Pacific explorer of the Solomons. Ventura Fuentes tells his voyages. He sought the isles of gold. His widow carried on the quest. Spain's sailor of the South Seas. His isles were lost for two centuries.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amadia-and-ak: A 1913 entry on Amadia and Akra — the Chaldean sees of Kurdistan. Sophrone Pétridès gives their mountain story. Nestorian Christians kept the ancient faith. Their hills hid the old churches. The East's highland dioceses. Their monks keep the Chaldean rite.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amra: A 1913 entry on the Amra — the Irish elegy for Columba. Arthur Ua Clerigh explains its fame. Dallan Forgaill sang the saint's praise. Its verses are Ireland's oldest. The Gael's great lament. Its language is old and obscure. Its praise outlived the poet.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anaphora: A 1913 entry on the anaphora — the great eucharistic prayer. Andrew Shipman unfolds its solemn structure. The East's liturgies center here. The words of institution crown the rite. The Church's high offering. Its epiclesis calls the Spirit down. Its chant lifts the people's hearts.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancient-see-o: This 1913 reference piece on the ancient see of Skara — Sweden's oldest bishopric. Arthur Taylor gives its story. Its bishops served the Göta lands. The Reformation ended the line. A vanished see of the Swedes. Its school is Sweden's oldest.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancyra: This 1913 reference article on Ancyra — Ankara, the city of the early councils. Thomas Shahan tells its church story. Its canons shaped the ancient discipline. The Galatian capital kept the faith. A council city of Asia Minor. Its canons bound the early clergy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-angora: This 1913 reference article on Angora — Ankara, the Anatolian city. Jules Pargoire tells its Christian past. Its councils shaped the ancient Church. The citadel watches the steppe town. Asia Minor's highland capital. Its cats are famed through Europe. Its mohair clothed the Ottoman court.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-angra: This 1913 reference piece on Angra — the Azores diocese. The entry tells its island story. Its cathedral faces the Atlantic harbor. The faith crossed with the settlers. A mid-ocean bishopric. Its fortress guarded the India fleets. Its streets keep the Manueline style.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ann-lobera: A 1913 entry on Ana de Lobera — St. Teresa's beloved companion. Benedict Zimmerman honors her fidelity. She shared the foundress's labors. The reform's trials tested her too. A saint's right hand. Her letters breathe the reform's spirit. Her counsel steadied the young houses.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antipater-of-: This 1913 reference article on Antipater of Bostra — the bishop against Eutyches. F.M. Rudge honors his orthodoxy. His pen defended the two natures. The council heard his voice. A prelate of the true faith. His see guarded the Hauran plain.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-ferre: A 1913 entry on Antonio Ferreira — the Portuguese poet of the Renaissance. Jeremiah Ford praises his Castro. His tragedy founded the national stage. Coimbra's muse crowned his verse. Portugal's classical poet. His odes sang the Tagus' praise. His Bristo graced the courtly stage.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-vieir: A 1913 entry on Antonio Vieira — the Portuguese Jesuit, preacher to kings and Indians. John Reville honors his mighty sermons. His voice shook the Lisbon court. Brazil's missions knew his zeal. The golden mouth of Portugal. His sermons fill the Portuguese classics.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostolic-cam: This 1913 reference piece on the Apostolic Camera — the papal treasury. Johann Peter Kirsch traces its medieval might. The camerlengo guards its coffers. The conclave's goods are his care. The exchequer of the Holy See. Its archives fill the Vatican vaults.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aymara: This 1913 reference piece on the Aymara — the Andean people of the high plateau. Adolph Bandelier describes their ancient towns. They built by Titicaca's shore. The missions tamed their highland pride. The people of the cold heights. Their totora boats float the lake.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-balthasar-bar: This 1913 reference piece on Balthasar Barreira — the Jesuit missionary of Angola. James Cotter honors his long labors. He served the African missions for decades. The Congo knew his zeal. A pioneer priest of the dark continent. His mission stood on the Kwanza.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-belem-do-para: A 1913 entry on Belém do Pará — the Amazonian archdiocese. Francisco Yanes gives its tropical story. Its bishops serve the river missions. The Nazinha draws the crowds. A see of the great river's mouth. Its Ver-o-Peso market charms visitors.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benedict-pere: This 1913 reference article on Benedict Pereira — the Jesuit theologian. Walter Drum honors his learned tomes. His disputations filled the Roman schools. The Society prized its doctor. A priest among the schoolmen. His order honors its theologian.
